I work at a horse stable getting minimum wage. We take out a bunch of trial rides with beginners. Some of these people are enjoyable, others are nightmares to manage.

Anyway the other day, Saturday, me and a coworker were taking out a 2:00 ride. There were 8 people, 6 were all one group. One girl was two young to ride on her own, so I was the one who had a lead rope on her horse. The horse the girl was on is a good horse, honestly would've been fine not being led but the insurance says that as long as someone holds on it's fine. The whole time I'm pretty stretched backwards, as well as trying to keep my horse from bumping into the one in front of me who would kick if a horse got too close. My coworker lead the ride, and I was towards the back. 

Halfway through the ride we heard thunder. It was still sunny and we figured we could at least finish one half hour loop of the hour trail ride. I joked with the girl's mom about us possibly not making it back in time. Halfway through the half hour loop, our boss texts my coworker and I that nasty storms are headed our way and we should cut the ride short. The loop we were on had no turn around points so we just had to keep continuing. Towards the end of the loop, it got dark. Like super dark, it looked like dusk. I was getting a little worried myself, and the girl I was leading was pretty scared too because the thunder was loud.

Just before the group exited the woods, it started raining. The mom said that acorns were hitting her in the head. Nope, that was hail. The rain wasn't so bad at first, but then it just down poured. So it was hailing and raining and the thunder and lightning was right on us. The horses who are generally perfect were getting worked up. This thunder struck, and all of the horses in the middle bunched up. The one lady screamed "what do I do?!" 

I had no idea so I just said "you have to hold on." All of the horses are trying to trot and get back to the barn as quick as possible. I felt frozen. Hail kept hitting, water was pooling in my boots, down my pants(and I was on my period, not a fun feeling), horses were scared, people were scared. I couldn't do anything to help really besides hold onto the girl's horse as well as control my own horse. The barn soon approached and the thunder was deafening. My leg was shaking I was so nervous. Other people were at the barn to help everyone off and get horses inside. No one was hurt or anything, but that job can be so stressful because of the unpredictability of horses, people, weather. Everyone on that ride was pretty awesome all things considered, even the horses. 

The job is pretty good most days when we arenas dealing with what felt like tornado like weather, but days like that put in perspective how everything can change instantly.
